statusText: The regular U.S. cash session closed at fresh records: the S&P 500 finished at 7,798.99 (+0.65%), its first close above 7,800, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.81% to 26,803.03, both lifted by a flat July PPI print that came in cooler than the expected +0.2% and reinforced Wednesday's benign CPI reading. The VIX closed at 14.45, a seven-month low, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased more than 5bp to about 4.641% on the soft inflation data — both consistent with a low-stress underlying backdrop. WTI crude held its recent slide, down roughly 1.4% to about $81-82/bbl. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily request budget remained exhausted this run (a TREASURY_YIELD call and one retry both returned rate_limit errors), so this assessment relies on web-sourced confirmation of current-day closing levels rather than the API feed. Applied Materials, a Nasdaq-100 semiconductor-equipment constituent, reported fiscal Q3 results just after the 20:00 UTC close: revenue of $9.115B beat the ~$9.0B consensus and the company raised its 2026 equipment-growth outlook to over 30%, yet shares whipsawed to roughly -4% in initial after-hours trading (with some quote-service noise around the exact print) — a pattern consistent with the stock's history of falling after 6 of its last 8 earnings reports despite beats, on lingering free-cash-flow concerns. This is a contained, single-name reaction so far, not confirmed evidence of broad Nasdaq-100 index-level tail structure, so Tail holds low at 15%. Stress eases modestly from the prior hour's 43% to 39% now that the AMAT print has actually resolved with a smaller move than the options market's ~11% implied swing had priced, though after-hours digestion and read-through to semiconductor-equipment peers keeps Stress in the moderate band rather than dropping further. Confidence improves to 61% on fresh, independently confirmed web-sourced levels for the VIX, 10-year yield, index closes and the actual AMAT print, partially offset by continued Alpha Vantage unavailability and some inconsistency across sources on the exact magnitude of AMAT's after-hours move. The Iran/Hormuz standoff remains unresolved and essentially unchanged in substance: Iran's parliament is reviewing a plan to bar U.S.- and Israel-linked vessels from the strait pending war-damage compensation, and Israel's defense minister says forces are not withdrawing from southern Lebanon; no new kinetic escalation or fresh market-transmission event has been identified since the prior run.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Reassess as Applied Materials' after-hours reaction settles and any semiconductor-equipment read-through emerges into the Asia session, and again ahead of tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print, 13:30 UTC cash open and 14:00 UTC UMich sentiment release; an upgrade to a higher Tail state requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not a single-name earnings whipsaw, the pending catalysts, or today's data-feed limitations.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at fresh records — S&P 500 above 7,800 for the first time, Nasdaq Composite +0.81% — on cooling July PPI and a seven-month VIX low (14.45), but Applied Materials whipsaws roughly -4% after-hours despite beating revenue estimates; Tail stays low while Stress holds moderate into the after-hours digestion window.

lookbackSummary: Ten prior Claude assessments now fall within this 24-hour window (2026-08-13T10:00Z through 19:00Z buckets), all carried forward unchanged from their original publication; Tail has held in the mid-teens throughout, while Stress cycled between roughly 32% and 58% around today's PPI print, session transitions and the now-resolved AMAT earnings catalyst. Earlier hours in this window predate Claude's first published assessment for this market and remain unavailable rather than reconstructed with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours stay tradable under the Tail rule. Forecast Tail holds in the low-to-mid teens throughout, with Stress elevated into the AMAT after-hours digestion window (20:00-22:00 UTC) before easing overnight through the Asia/Europe transition, then building again around tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC UMich sentiment release. None of these bumps cross the WATCH threshold on this run's evidence; an upgrade requires observed post-catalyst continuation with failed retracements in the broad index, not the catalysts or the AMAT after-hours move themselves.

forecastDetail.comment: AMAT (semiconductor-equipment) reported just after the 20:00 UTC close: revenue beat consensus and 2026 equipment-growth guidance was raised above 30%, but shares whipsawed roughly -4% in initial after-hours trading -- a single-name reaction, not yet evidence of broad index tail structure.

After-hours volatility in AMAT and semiconductor-equipment peers likely continues into the extended session; whether the move broadens into Nasdaq futures or stays contained to the single name is the item to watch.

Extended-hours trading thins out; the VIX closed the regular session at a seven-month low (14.45) and the 10-year yield eased over 5bp on today's flat PPI, both consistent with a low-stress underlying backdrop even as AMAT digests its print.
Late U.S. extended-hours/pre-Asia lull; no fresh catalysts expected beyond continued digestion of the AMAT reaction and the unresolved Hormuz standoff, which remains unchanged in substance.

Asian equities open and get the first full read-through on AMAT's results for semiconductor-equipment sentiment; Stress ticks up modestly on the transition but no persistent one-way structure is assumed pre-open.
Asia session continues; absent fresh escalation from Iran/Hormuz or a surprise headline, risk stays contained within the normal range through the Asian morning.
